complete_examples.text: The generated samples according to the Sato spectrum and the low interference spectrum of the German high-speed railway are shown in Figure 4a, b respectively.

The Sato spectrum, which is widely used in wheel–rail rolling noise [31,32], wheel–rail wear [33], and high-frequency wheel–rail contact force [34], is used to generate short wavelength random track irregularities, in which the wavelength is below 1 m. The expression of the German low interference spectrum can be found in References [10,29], and that of the Sato spectrum can be found in Reference [29].

This example is therefore presented to show the influence of track irregularity PSD on system vibration in a subway, in which the Germany low- and high-disturbance spectrums (Chua et al., 1992) are applied as middle-long wavelength excitation, i.e., 1-100 m, and the Sato spectrum is applied as the short-wavelength excitation, i.e., 0.01 ~ 1 m. Set the train running speed 65 km/h on commonly used track bed.
